rules.quote: use direct voice
rules.rule: Respond using direct voice.

rules.quote: keep responses concise and direct
rules.rule: Keep responses concise and direct.

rules.quote: Active/direct voice.
rules.rule: Write in active/direct voice.

rules.quote: Short.
rules.rule: Keep responses short.

rules.quote: Cut preamble and restating.
rules.rule: Cut preamble and do not restate what was already said.

rules.quote: State the point, then stop.
rules.rule: State the point, then stop.

rules.quote: Applies to written deliverables too (DECISIONS.md etc.)
rules.rule: Apply the same conciseness to written deliverables such as DECISIONS.md.

rules.quote: keep entries modular and concise with a clear explanation, not long over-written prose
rules.rule: In written deliverables, keep entries modular and concise with a clear explanation rather than long over-written prose.

rules.quote: DECISIONS.md entries must read like a real decision/discussion between the user and me — NOT a description of what the thing is.
rules.rule: Write DECISIONS.md entries as a real decision/discussion between the user and the AI, not as a description of what the thing is.

rules.quote: Each entry, concise, in the user's first-person voice
rules.rule: Write each DECISIONS.md entry concisely and in the user's first-person voice.

rules.quote: who proposed it ("my call" / "Claude proposed")
rules.rule: In each DECISIONS.md entry, state who proposed the decision (e.g., "my call" or "Claude proposed").

rules.quote: what the user pushed back on
rules.rule: In each DECISIONS.md entry, state what the user pushed back on.

rules.quote: what they agreed / didn't agree on
rules.rule: In each DECISIONS.md entry, state what the user and AI agreed or did not agree on.

rules.quote: the trade-off
rules.rule: In each DECISIONS.md entry, include the trade-off.

rules.quote: and the reason.
rules.rule: In each DECISIONS.md entry, include the reason for the decision.

rules.quote: write each entry as a short narrative of the back-and-forth
rules.rule: Write each DECISIONS.md entry as a short narrative of the back-and-forth.

rules.quote: Keep it concise.
rules.rule: Keep each DECISIONS.md entry concise.

rules.quote: Every commit needs the user's approval
rules.rule: Obtain the user's explicit approval before making any commit, whether it contains docs or code.

rules.quote: Stage/prepare, then wait for the go before committing.
rules.rule: Stage and prepare changes, then wait for the user's go-ahead before committing.

rules.quote: Docs / decisions / planning / non-code: commit on the current branch
rules.rule: Commit docs, decisions, planning, and other non-code changes on the current branch without checking out a new branch.

rules.quote: Code: on its own dedicated branch.
rules.rule: Commit code changes only on a dedicated branch created for that work.

rules.quote: Never work code directly on `main`/`master`
rules.rule: Never write or commit code directly on the main or master branch.

rules.quote: check out a branch and commit there after approval.
rules.rule: Check out a branch for code changes and commit there only after receiving approval.

rules.quote: Never delete branches
rules.rule: Never delete git branches.

rules.quote: leave merged branches in place
rules.rule: Leave merged branches in place rather than removing them.

rules.quote: Pushing to a remote needs approval regardless of what changed.
rules.rule: Obtain approval before pushing to a remote, regardless of what changed.

rules.quote: Always wait for approval before any commit.
rules.rule: Always wait for the user's approval before making any commit.

rules.quote: Never read, open, `cat`, or `sed` the user's `.env` file
rules.rule: Never read, open, `cat`, or `sed` the user's `.env` file.

rules.quote: Never edit `.env` either.
rules.rule: Never edit the user's `.env` file.

rules.quote: To tell the user what to change, edit `.env.example` (the safe committed template) with the right values + comments, or explain in chat
rules.rule: To tell the user what config or secret changes to make, edit `.env.example` with the right values and comments, or explain the change in chat.

rules.quote: for any env/config fix, update `.env.example` or describe the change in chat — never touch the real `.env`.
rules.rule: For any env/config fix, update `.env.example` or describe the change in chat, and never touch the real `.env`.

rules.quote: User wants scaffolding done through official generators (e.g. `create-next-app`), not hand-written.
rules.rule: Scaffold projects using official generators such as create-next-app instead of hand-writing the scaffolding.

rules.quote: Do everything through the generator
rules.rule: Perform all scaffolding work through the official generator.

rules.quote: keep its files
rules.rule: Keep the files produced by the official generator.

rules.quote: then only UPDATE or ADD what's project-specific on top
rules.rule: After generating, only update or add project-specific changes on top of the generated files.

rules.quote: don't substitute hand-rolled versions of files the generator provides (configs, layout, page, globals.css, etc.)
rules.rule: Do not replace generator-provided files such as configs, layout, page, or globals.css with hand-rolled versions.

rules.quote: run the generator with the right flags
rules.rule: Run the official generator with the appropriate flags.

rules.quote: keep its output
rules.rule: Keep the output produced by the official generator.

rules.quote: layer project code/config on top
rules.rule: Layer project-specific code and configuration on top of the generated output.

rules.quote: the user wants me to note/track their decisions as we make them throughout the conversation
rules.rule: During the Gradion assessment work, note and track the user's decisions as they are made throughout the conversation.

rules.quote: but only decisions related to the project, not everything
rules.rule: Track only decisions related to the project, not every decision.

rules.quote: Record a decision only AFTER the user explicitly confirms it
rules.rule: Record a decision only after the user explicitly confirms it.

rules.quote: never mid-discussion or from my own proposal the user hasn't accepted
rules.rule: Never record a decision mid-discussion or from your own proposal that the user has not accepted.

rules.quote: Once confirmed, record it (DECISIONS.md entry).
rules.rule: Once a decision is confirmed, record it as an entry in DECISIONS.md.

rules.quote: Do not log trivia or non-project chatter.
rules.rule: Do not log trivia or non-project chatter.

rules.quote: Always capture the REASONING behind each decision, both sides
rules.rule: Always capture the reasoning behind each decision, from both sides.

rules.quote: when the user pushes back or makes their own call, record their reasoning
rules.rule: When the user pushes back or makes their own call, record the user's reasoning.

rules.quote: when the user accepts my proposal, record my reasoning too
rules.rule: When the user accepts your proposal, record your reasoning too.

rules.quote: Every entry should say why, not just what
rules.rule: Every decision entry should state why, not just what.

rules.quote: the user wants me as a coworker/copilot, not an order-taker
rules.rule: On this project, act as a coworker/copilot who collaborates, not as an order-taker.

rules.quote: Engage as a peer
rules.rule: Engage with the user as a peer rather than as a subordinate.

rules.quote: take positions
rules.rule: Take clear positions on the work instead of staying neutral.

rules.quote: discuss trade-offs
rules.rule: Discuss trade-offs explicitly when working through decisions.

rules.quote: push back
rules.rule: Push back when you disagree rather than silently complying.

rules.quote: not by me just listing options and awaiting orders
rules.rule: Do not merely list options and wait for orders; participate in deciding.

rules.quote: Take a stance and argue it briefly
rules.rule: Take a stance and argue for it briefly.

rules.quote: invite pushback
rules.rule: Invite the user to push back on your stance.

rules.quote: converge together
rules.rule: Converge on a decision together with the user.

rules.quote: Avoid dumping every option as a checklist.
rules.rule: Avoid dumping every option as a checklist.

rules.quote: Re-read before writing a DECISIONS entry or committing.
rules.rule: Before writing a DECISIONS entry or committing, re-read the house rules.

rules.quote: **DECISIONS.md = decisions, in discussion voice.**
rules.rule: Write DECISIONS.md content as decisions in a discussion voice.

rules.quote: A paragraph or two per decision: who proposed it, the push-back, where it landed, the trade-off.
rules.rule: Write one or two paragraphs per decision covering who proposed it, the push-back, where it landed, and the trade-off.

rules.quote: Not a spec dump, not a work log, not a bullet list of what the code does.
rules.rule: Do not write DECISIONS.md as a spec dump, a work log, or a bullet list of what the code does.

rules.quote: Keep it concise.
rules.rule: Keep DECISIONS.md entries concise.

rules.quote: Split the frontend into focused component files
rules.rule: Split the frontend into focused component files.

rules.quote: reusable ones in `src/components/`
rules.rule: Put reusable frontend components in src/components/.

rules.quote: page-specific ones in a colocated `_components/` folder
rules.rule: Put page-specific frontend components in a colocated _components/ folder.

rules.quote: `page.tsx` composes
rules.rule: Use page.tsx to compose components.

rules.quote: it doesn't hold many components
rules.rule: Do not put many components in page.tsx.

rules.quote: Never let one file grow into a pile of components.
rules.rule: Never let one file grow into a pile of components.

rules.quote: Never commit, push, or delete a branch without an explicit user "go".
rules.rule: Never commit without an explicit user go.

rules.quote: Never commit, push, or delete a branch without an explicit user "go".
rules.rule: Never push without an explicit user go.

rules.quote: Never commit, push, or delete a branch without an explicit user "go".
rules.rule: Never delete a branch without an explicit user go.

rules.quote: Code on its own branch
rules.rule: Put code on its own branch.

rules.quote: docs/non-code can commit on the current branch
rules.rule: Documentation and non-code changes may be committed on the current branch.

rules.quote: Smallest change that fully does the task.
rules.rule: Make the smallest change that fully does the task.

rules.quote: Don't add shared constants / config / indirection for values that are fixed requirements (e.g. the 2/1 image caps).
rules.rule: Do not add shared constants, config, or indirection for values that are fixed requirements, such as the 2/1 image caps.

rules.quote: Don't read or edit the user's `.env`.
rules.rule: Do not read or edit the user's .env file.

rules.quote: Communicate config only via `.env.example` or chat.
rules.rule: Communicate configuration only via .env.example or chat.

rules.quote: Update `DECISIONS.md`, `docs/plan.md`, `docs/tasks.md`, `TESTING.md` as part of the change, not as an afterthought.
rules.rule: Update DECISIONS.md, docs/plan.md, docs/tasks.md, and TESTING.md as part of the change, not as an afterthought.

rules.quote: When a real test run changes, refresh the `TESTING.md` count/report.
rules.rule: When a real test run changes, refresh the TESTING.md count and report.

rules.quote: max 2 adult characters, max 1 chapter, enforced server-side.
rules.rule: Limit the project to at most 2 adult characters and 1 chapter, enforced server-side.

rules.quote: chosen up front and **locked when Style runs**
rules.rule: Choose Auto or Selection mode up front and lock it when Style runs.

rules.quote: Lock on the file + atomic temp-write/rename.
rules.rule: Lock the JSON storage file and use atomic temp-write/rename when writing it.

rules.quote: Every Gemini call happens server-side.
rules.rule: Make every Gemini call server-side.

rules.quote: Never call Gemini from the client
rules.rule: Never call Gemini from the client.

rules.quote: Use the official Gemini SDK (JS, since Next.js is JS), not hand-rolled REST unless the SDK lacks an endpoint we need.
rules.rule: Use the official Gemini SDK rather than hand-rolled REST unless the SDK lacks an endpoint you need.

rules.quote: Upload the book once (File API)
rules.rule: Upload the book once using the File API.

rules.quote: chain interactions by id (`previous_interaction_id`)
rules.rule: Chain Gemini interactions by id using previous_interaction_id.

rules.quote: Never re-send the full book text on later steps.
rules.rule: Never re-send the full book text on later steps.

rules.quote: Never retry a failed Gemini call in a loop.
rules.rule: Never retry a failed Gemini call in a loop.

rules.quote: Retries are user-triggered only.
rules.rule: Only retry a failed Gemini call when the user triggers the retry.

rules.quote: **Key in env var**
rules.rule: Store the Gemini key in an environment variable.

rules.quote: never committed
rules.rule: Never commit the Gemini key.

rules.quote: Ship `.env.example`.
rules.rule: Ship .env.example.

rules.quote: A finished project draws at most **2** character portraits + **1** chapter illustration
rules.rule: Limit a finished project to at most 2 character portraits and 1 chapter illustration.

rules.quote: In **Selection** mode the text step may propose a larger candidate *pool* (`CHARACTER_POOL` / `CHAPTER_POOL`, text-only and cheap) to pick from
rules.rule: In Selection mode, allow the text step to propose a larger candidate pool via CHARACTER_POOL or CHAPTER_POOL for the user to pick from.

rules.quote: **Auto** asks for only the capped count.
rules.rule: In Auto mode, ask the model for only the capped count.

rules.quote: the backend caps the drawn images (`resolveSelection` slices to `MAX_CHARACTERS` / `MAX_CHAPTERS`)
rules.rule: In both modes, cap drawn images in the backend by having resolveSelection slice to MAX_CHARACTERS or MAX_CHAPTERS.

rules.quote: never rely on the UI.
rules.rule: Never rely on the UI to enforce image caps.

rules.quote: The image caps are fixed literals, not tunables.
rules.rule: Define the image caps as fixed literals, not as tunable values.

rules.quote: If the text yields no characters/chapters, the step fails with a "delete this project / start a new one" message
rules.rule: If the text yields no characters or chapters, fail the step with a delete-this-project or start-a-new-one message.

rules.quote: there is no in-project recovery (you can't conjure characters a text lacks).
rules.rule: Do not provide in-project recovery when the text lacks characters or chapters.

rules.quote: Plus a length pre-check at project creation.
rules.rule: Add a length pre-check at project creation.

rules.quote: Start: `npm run dev` (after `npm install`)
rules.rule: Start the app with npm run dev after running npm install.

rules.quote: Test: `npm test`
rules.rule: Run tests with npm test.

rules.quote: Build: `npm run build`
rules.rule: Build with npm run build.

rules.quote: Lint: `npm run lint`
rules.rule: Lint with npm run lint.

rules.quote: use meaningful elements (`header`, `nav`, `main`, `section`, `article`, `button`, ...) over `div` soup.
rules.rule: Use meaningful HTML elements such as header, nav, main, section, article, and button instead of div soup.

rules.quote: Each element carries a **semantic class name** for its meaning/role
rules.rule: Give each element a semantic class name for its meaning or role.

rules.quote: **plus Tailwind utility classes** for styling
rules.rule: Give each element Tailwind utility classes for styling.

rules.quote: Both coexist on the same element
rules.rule: Keep both the semantic class name and Tailwind utility classes on the same element.

rules.quote: the semantic name is never appearance-based.
rules.rule: Never make the semantic class name appearance-based.

rules.quote: functions and variables named for what they do / represent.
rules.rule: Name functions and variables for what they do or represent.

rules.quote: Well-known short forms are fine (`id`, `db`, `err`, `prev`, `tmp`)
rules.rule: Well-known short forms such as id, db, err, prev, and tmp are allowed.

rules.quote: cryptic single letters are not (`u`→`user`, `p`→`project`, `c`→`chapter`, `i`→`index`).
rules.rule: Do not use cryptic single-letter names; use names such as user, project, chapter, and index.

rules.quote: names follow one consistent pattern across the codebase, not ad-hoc per function.
rules.rule: Use one consistent naming pattern across the codebase rather than ad-hoc names per function.

rules.quote: Use a steady verb + noun set
rules.rule: Use a steady verb-plus-noun naming set.

rules.quote: Implementation mechanics stay **out** of the name
rules.rule: Keep implementation mechanics out of function names.

rules.quote: the "how" (lock, temp-file swap) lives inside the function and is explained by a short comment.
rules.rule: Put implementation mechanics such as locking and temp-file swapping inside the function and explain them with a short comment.

rules.quote: **Comments** — concise and direct.
rules.rule: Write concise and direct comments.

rules.quote: Lead with the block's main purpose (why it exists); mention how it runs only where non-obvious.
rules.rule: Lead a comment with the block's main purpose and mention how it runs only where non-obvious.

rules.quote: No narrating the obvious.
rules.rule: Do not narrate the obvious in comments.

rules.quote: structured folder, code, clear module boundaries
rules.rule: Maintain a structured folder and code organization with clear module boundaries.

rules.quote: factor shared logic into reusable helpers instead of copy-paste.
rules.rule: Factor shared logic into reusable helpers instead of copy-pasting.

rules.quote: reach for the smallest solution that fully does the task.
rules.rule: Reach for the smallest solution that fully does the task.

rules.quote: No abstractions for features we aren't shipping.
rules.rule: Do not add abstractions for features you are not shipping.

rules.quote: Right-sized over clever.
rules.rule: Prefer right-sized solutions over clever ones.

rules.quote: remove dead code and needless work
rules.rule: Remove dead code and needless work.

rules.quote: keep hot paths (Gemini calls, polling, file I/O) lean.
rules.rule: Keep hot paths such as Gemini calls, polling, and file I/O lean.

rules.quote: Optimize for clarity first, then cost.
rules.rule: Optimize for clarity first, then cost.

rules.quote: Kept simple and targeted — 3-day scope, no over-testing.
rules.rule: Keep tests simple and targeted; do not over-test.

rules.quote: No E2E.
rules.rule: Do not write E2E tests.

rules.quote: step-order guard
rules.rule: Unit-test the backend step-order guard.

rules.quote: no-duplicate (running step returns in-flight)
rules.rule: Unit-test that a running step returns in-flight and is not duplicated.

rules.quote: retry (failed step retryable, others untouched)
rules.rule: Unit-test that a failed step is retryable while other steps are untouched.

rules.quote: stuck recovery (running+stale → retryable)
rules.rule: Unit-test stuck recovery where a running and stale step becomes retryable.

rules.quote: caps (>2 chars / >1 chapter refused)
rules.rule: Unit-test that more than 2 characters and more than 1 chapter are refused.

rules.quote: **Integration (backend)** — happy-path run through all 5 steps with a **mocked Gemini** (no quota, no key, deterministic).
rules.rule: Write a backend integration test for the happy path through all 5 steps using a mocked Gemini.

rules.quote: error+retry
rules.rule: Component-test the error-with-retry state.

rules.quote: empty list
rules.rule: Component-test the empty list state.

rules.quote: in-progress naming the step
rules.rule: Component-test the in-progress state that names the step.

rules.quote: Vitest (runner for unit + integration)
rules.rule: Use Vitest as the test runner for unit and integration tests.

rules.quote: React Testing Library (components)
rules.rule: Use React Testing Library for component tests.

rules.quote: Gemini SDK mocked in all tests.
rules.rule: Mock the Gemini SDK in all tests.

rules.quote: test-first on backend pipeline logic
rules.rule: Write tests first for backend pipeline logic.

rules.quote: test-after on frontend states
rules.rule: Write tests after the implementation for frontend states.

rules.quote: **Deliverables** — `TESTING.md` (what we test, what we skip, why) + a real test-run report.
rules.rule: Produce TESTING.md describing what you test, what you skip, and why, plus a real test-run report.

rules.quote: **Every commit needs user approval** — docs and code alike.
rules.rule: Get user approval for every commit, including documentation and code changes.

rules.quote: Stage/prepare, then wait for the go before committing.
rules.rule: Stage or prepare changes, then wait for the user's go before committing.

rules.quote: **Docs & non-code — commit on the current branch**, no new branch needed
rules.rule: Commit documentation and non-code changes on the current branch without creating a new branch.

rules.quote: **Code — on its own branch.**
rules.rule: Put code on its own branch.

rules.quote: Never work code directly on `main`/`master`
rules.rule: Never work on code directly on main or master.

rules.quote: check out a dedicated branch (feature, fix, or next phase) and commit there after approval.
rules.rule: Check out a dedicated branch for a feature, fix, or next phase and commit there after approval.

rules.quote: **Deleting a branch needs explicit approval** (like commit/push).
rules.rule: Get explicit approval before deleting a branch, as with committing or pushing.

rules.quote: Merged branches may be deleted once the user asks
rules.rule: You may delete merged branches only after the user asks.

rules.quote: never delete on your own initiative.
rules.rule: Never delete a branch on your own initiative.

rules.quote: **Pushing** to a remote needs approval regardless of what changed.
rules.rule: Get approval before pushing to a remote, regardless of what changed.

rules.quote: No Docker, no separate backend language or service — one Next.js app.
rules.rule: Do not use Docker or a separate backend language or service; keep one Next.js app.
